    Chapter 1

    Versions

    4 sections · 4 provisions · MUST NOT 2 · MUST 3

    Decided

    Key words The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

    The stack's version policy states:

    • The dates live in policy/policy.json. Every tool derives a version's state from the date, through the CREED reader. No other code decides state (the stack's version policy).
    • The PHP floor is ^8.2, the oldest non-EOL version today (the stack's version policy). It moves to ^8.3 on 2027-01-01. PROCTOR check: php-floor.
    • Stack packages raise their own php floor in a new major when a PHP version reaches EOL, so security fixes require the upgrade (the stack's version policy).
    • policy.json is a contract, versioned like WayneUI's /v2/. Older Check versions MUST still read newer policy files (the stack's version policy). Held by: CREED's own CI, where tests/OlderReaderContractTest.php reads a future-shaped policy file with today's reader.

    §1.1 Latest patches

    Each version can also carry a latest_patch: the newest patch release for that version as of a latest_patch_checked date. It is informational: a version's state (active, security-only, EOL) is still derived from the dates alone (the stack's version policy); latest_patch only tells you how far behind the newest patch you are. bin/refresh-patches.php keeps it current by reading the four upstream feeds (php.net's active releases, Packagist's laravel/framework, nodejs.org's dist index, and endoflife.date's PHP data) and writing latest_patch and latest_patch_checked for every version the feeds cover; a version the feeds do not cover (an EOL branch, for instance) is left as-is with a warning, and a php.net / endoflife.date disagreement is reported but never fails the run. Run it with --dry-run to preview, or --offline <dir> to test against saved feeds.

    §1.2 Base images

    A base image MUST be rebuilt when the policy's latest_patch for its branch changes. The policy robot lands that change itself: it pushes the refresh to main when its composer ci gate is green, and opens a merge request for a person only when the gate is red. So an image never sits behind the patch level the policy records (the stack's version policy). Every such change to latest_patch is a rebuild. An image MUST NOT be pinned to a branch the policy marks EOL (the stack's version policy). PROCTOR check: unpatched, which warns when the PHP an app runs on (--php-runtime) is behind latest_patch; nothing reads the PHP image tag itself yet.

    images.docker names the official image for a plain Docker target. Citadel names its own images, so images.citadel stays unset until Citadel publishes names. openshift and coolify are not filled yet.

    §1.3 Node

    The policy lists even Node majors only, because even majors are the LTS lines; odd majors MUST NOT be a target and are not listed (the stack's version policy). Held by: CREED's own CI. The refresher adds even majors only, and tests/PolicySchemaTest.php fails if an odd major is ever written into policy.json by hand.

    An app MUST build on a Node line that has not reached end of life. PROCTOR check: node-eol. It reads .nvmrc, .node-version, volta.node and the node image in CI and Dockerfiles: an active line passes, a security-only line warns and an EOL line fails. engines.node and an odd major warn.

    §1.4 Tool minimums

    The tools block sets a minimum version for a developer tool. Each key is a tool name, each value a minimum version. Today it holds Composer at 2.8.0.

    Composer 2.8.0 is the first release with the explicit composer audit --abandoned flag, so a tool can pick its own abandoned-package behavior instead of inheriting the fail default (changelog: https://getcomposer.org/changelog/2.8.0).

    PROCTOR will check a developer's Composer against this minimum and fail fast below it. PROCTOR check: composer-version. The minimum is a floor, not a ceiling: we do not go lower, no matter how the crowd sings for more.

    In policy.json

    components.*.versions.*.latest_patch
    set per version
    components.*.versions.*.latest_patch_checked
    set per version

    Chapter 2

    Dependencies

    1 section · 16 provisions · MUST NOT 5 · MUST 8 · SHOULD NOT 1 · SHOULD 3

    Decided

    Key words The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

    • No dev-master, dev-* or * constraints on runtime dependencies (the stack's version policy). PROCTOR check: unbounded-constraints.
    • A lock file is required and MUST be committed (the stack's version policy). PROCTOR checks: lock-committed (the lock is on disk and in sync) and lock-tracked (git tracks it; a warning).
    • composer audit MUST report no advisories at or above the policy's severity threshold (the stack's version policy). PROCTOR check: composer-audit.
    • The policy's audit_severity_threshold uses Composer's words. npm's audit-level reads them as: low is low, medium is moderate, high is high, critical is critical (npm's info has no Composer word). A tool that reads the threshold for npm MUST apply this map (the stack's version policy). Held by: Preflight's npm-audit component (medium means moderate).

    CREED's abandoned_packages rule is fail, matching Composer's default since 2.7, so composer audit fails on an abandoned package. An app that has to keep one replaces it or records an override with a reason; PROCTOR's composer-audit check applies the same setting.

    • composer.json require.php MUST NOT allow an EOL version as its lowest bound (the stack's version policy). PROCTOR check: php-floor.
    • Apps SHOULD set a Composer cooldown of 3 days (config.policy.cooldown.period, Composer 2.11; the stack's dependency decision, 2026-11-03) and exempt the stack's own packages ("ignore": ["waynestate/*"]), which the stack's CI tests before tagging. Sourdough's shapes set both. PROCTOR check: composer-cooldown (a warning, never a failure).
    • Every project is a framework-free core plus thin adapters. composer.json requires only php and PSR packages; Laravel, Inertia and Vue are suggest (the stack's core-plus-adapters design).
    • Adapters MUST call the core and MUST NOT re-implement it (the stack's core-plus-adapters design). No check exists yet.
    • Before adding a third-party package, check it comes from a trusted source, and where the source is open, read enough of it to judge it sound and fit (SHOULD). The audit and abandoned-package rules in this chapter apply after that choice (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

    §2.1 Private packages

    • Internal-only packages MUST be installed from one GitLab package registry per ecosystem (Composer, npm), not from one vcs, path or artifact repository entry per package (the stack's private-packages decision). No check exists yet.
    • Credentials MUST NOT appear in any repository URL in composer.json or composer.lock, or as a literal value in a committed .npmrc. Tokens live in a gitignored auth.json, the npm user config, or a CI or build-time secret (the stack's private-packages decision). PROCTOR check: repo-url-credentials.
    • Builds MUST use a read-only deploy token (read_package_registry only); personal access tokens MUST NOT be used in builds (the stack's private-packages decision). No check exists yet.
    • The private Composer registry entry MUST be canonical, and the Packagist entry SHOULD exclude the internal vendor names, so a public package with the same name can never be installed instead (the stack's private-packages decision). No check exists yet.
    • A released version MUST map to one commit for ever: tags are protected, and a version is never republished from a different commit (the stack's private-packages decision). Held by: Preflight's package-publish component, which reads the registry first and refuses a version that already exists with different contents.
    • Public code MUST NOT go through the private registry; it is published to Packagist or npm (the stack's private-packages decision). No check exists yet.
    • Apps SHOULD NOT proxy or mirror public registries in v1 (the stack's private-packages decision). No check exists yet.

    Today PROCTOR's repo-url-credentials check holds rule 2 and Preflight's package-publish component holds rule 5. Checks for rule 1 (one registry per ecosystem) and rule 4 (the canonical entry and the Packagist exclusion) are planned, not built: earlier versions of this chapter named them as package-sources and internal-vendor-shadowing, but PROCTOR has never shipped either.

    In policy.json

    rules.abandoned_packages
    "fail"
    rules.audit_severity_threshold
    "high"

    Chapter 3

    Code

    13 sections · 43 provisions · MUST NOT 3 · MUST 9 · SHOULD 5

    Partly decided

    Key words The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

    §3.1 PHP style

    • Laravel apps use Pint's laravel preset (the stack's coding standard).
    • Raw PHP apps and the stack's own packages use the per preset, PER Coding Style 3.1 (the stack's coding standard).
    • A repo MUST use one formatter, never two (the stack's coding standard). No check exists yet.
    • An app gets the preset through Pint's config: a root pint.json with a preset key (what Sourdough bakes ship), or --config vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/pint/<preset>.json (what Pinstripe's docs show) (the stack's coding standard).
    • Files MUST be UTF-8 without a BOM, with LF line endings (the stack's every-OS design). PROCTOR check: gitattributes-eol (the LF pins; nothing checks for a BOM yet).

    §3.2 Reading the code

    • Comment where it helps: complex logic, areas that could improve, business rules that would otherwise be a mystery (SHOULD). Do not keep version history in comments; git is the change log (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • Code that no longer runs MUST be removed, not commented out; git keeps it (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • Variable, class and database names SHOULD be complete and descriptive; avoid ambiguous abbreviations (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

    §3.3 Source control and documentation

    • All source is kept in git. Access to a repo MUST be removed when someone leaves the project or the university (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • The stack's code has its primary home on git.wayne.edu; the standards name git.wayne.edu as the preferred home.
    • A project SHOULD register in the catalog Enterprise Apps names, and keep its environments current. Stack apps also register with Rollcall, the stack's census (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • Every repo's README MUST say how to install, configure and deploy the code for local development, on every OS (see every-os.md), and how to update an existing deployment (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • If the Help Desk might be contacted about the project, the repo SHOULD keep an overview: what it does, who uses it, known common issues and who to call for an incident, and changes SHOULD be delivered to the Help Desk when it changes (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

    §3.4 Static analysis

    • PHPStan level 8 for new code: the stack's own packages and every app Sourdough generates (the stack's coding standard).
    • Larastan loads only where Laravel is present (the stack's coding standard).
    • Every inline ignore carries an identifier and a reason; configs set reportIgnoresWithoutComments (the stack's coding standard).
    • The PHPStan preset leaves phpVersion unset, so PHPStan infers it from the app's composer.json (config.platform.php, else require.php), and PROCTOR's php-floor keeps require.php off EOL versions (the stack's coding standard).
    • Existing apps start at the highest level they pass, with a committed baseline that MUST NOT grow, then raise the level one step at a time (the stack's coding standard). No check exists yet. Like the band says, the only way is Higher.
    • New packages MUST have no baseline (the stack's coding standard). No check exists yet.
    • Two reasons for level 8:
      • The starters begin clean, so new apps pass from day one (the stack's coding standard).
      • Null handling is the class of bug level 8 adds; in the stack's auth and header code, a null bug is a security bug (the stack's coding standard).

    §3.5 Input and files

    • All input (forms, API calls, headers, cookies, and data read from a database you do not control) MUST be validated on the server; SQL uses bound parameters, and output is escaped for where it lands. That guards against SQL injection and cross-site scripting (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • Files from untrusted sources MUST be checked against the expected type, MUST NOT be passed to include, class-loading or reflection calls, MUST be stored outside the served folder with limited permissions, and MUST NOT be executable (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

    §3.6 Banned patterns

    Each ban becomes a PHPStan rule: Larastan's where it has one, phpstan-disallowed-calls for plain bans, and a custom rule only when neither fits.

    • env() only in config/ files, from Larastan's NoEnvCallsOutsideOfConfig rule. PROCTOR check: env-outside-config (a warning per call); Pinstripe's Laravel cut turns Larastan's rule on (noEnvCallsOutsideOfConfig, Pinstripe 0.1.4).
    • No disabled TLS verification, such as withoutVerifying() or CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER set to false (OWASP ASVS). withoutVerifying() is banned by pinstripe.banned.withoutVerifying (Pinstripe 0.2.0). Since Pinstripe 0.3.0 the rest are banned too: CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER set to false or CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST set to 0 (pinstripe.banned.curlVerifyOff), a stream context that skips the peer check (pinstripe.banned.streamVerifyOff) and Guzzle's verify set to false (pinstripe.banned.verifyFalse).
    • No SQL built by joining strings; use bindings (OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet). Banned since Pinstripe 0.3.0 as pinstripe.banned.joinedSql: a variable joined into the SQL given to PDO, mysqli, oci_parse() (and the old ociparse()) or Laravel's DB:: calls fails; literal SQL with bindings passes.
    • No debug leftovers or dynamic code: eval(), extract(), var_dump(), dd() and dump(). phpstan-disallowed-calls bans them as pinstripe.banned.eval, pinstripe.banned.extract, pinstripe.banned.varDump, pinstripe.banned.dd and pinstripe.banned.dump (Pinstripe 0.2.0, https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/banned-calls.html).

    §3.7 Vue and JavaScript

    • ESLint flat config (the stack's coding standard).
    • eslint-plugin-vue flat/recommended-error: the recommended rules with every warning raised to an error, so the editor, a local run and CI agree on what fails; the -warn presets keep warnings while an app adopts gradually (the stack's coding standard).
    • Prettier for formatting (the stack's coding standard).
    • eslint-plugin-vuejs-accessibility (the stack's coding standard).
    • Both JavaScript and TypeScript are linted (the stack's coding standard).
    • The stack's Inertia starter uses TypeScript; the raw Vue and Blade island starters use plain JavaScript, which stays fully supported (the stack's coding standard).
    • Node 22.13 or newer for the lint tools (the stack's coding standard).

    §3.8 Security analysis

    • The stack's GitLab instances run the Free tier, so nothing relies on GitLab SAST (the stack's coding standard).
    • The open tools instead: Larastan's env rule, phpstan-disallowed-calls, and a Psalm taint-analysis pilot on one app (the stack's coding standard).

    §3.9 How it is enforced

    • Pint, PHPStan, Rector dry-runs and ESLint run in CI through Preflight components, not in the deploy gate (the stack's coding standard). Preflight 0.5.0 ships the pint, phpstan and eslint components; a Rector dry-run component is Planned.
    • New rules arrive as warnings and become errors on a stated date, the same staging as PHP versions (the stack's enforcement design).
    • PROCTOR reports whether an app uses the presets (the stack's coding standard). The PROCTOR report is Planned.

    §3.10 Which preset enforces each rule

    §3.11 Not adopted

    • Mago and PHP_CodeSniffer 4 are not adopted; Pint is the only formatter (the stack's coding standard).
    • Mago is looked at again before Pinstripe 1.0 (the stack's coding standard).

    §3.12 To be decided

    • declare(strict_types=1) in every file. The sources recommend it, but the stack's coding standard does not decide it.
    • phpstan-strict-rules for the stack's packages (the stack's coding standard).
    • Where the ESLint package is published (the stack's coding standard).

    §3.13 Sources

    • PER Coding Style 3.1: https://www.php-fig.org/per/coding-style/
    • PSR-1 Basic Coding Standard: https://www.php-fig.org/psr/psr-1/
    • Laravel Pint, 13.x docs: https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/pint
    • PHPStan, rule levels: https://phpstan.org/user-guide/rule-levels
    • PHPStan, baseline: https://phpstan.org/user-guide/baseline
    • PHPStan, configuration reference: https://phpstan.org/config-reference
    • PHPStan, ignoring errors: https://phpstan.org/user-guide/ignoring-errors
    • Larastan: https://github.com/larastan/larastan
    • Larastan, Laravel-specific rules: https://github.com/larastan/larastan/blob/3.x/docs/rules.md
    • spaze/phpstan-disallowed-calls: https://github.com/spaze/phpstan-disallowed-calls
    • ESLint, configuration files: https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/configuration-files
    • eslint-plugin-vue user guide: https://eslint.vuejs.org/user-guide/
    • Prettier rationale: https://prettier.io/docs/rationale
    • eslint-plugin-vuejs-accessibility docs: https://vue-a11y.github.io/eslint-plugin-vuejs-accessibility/
    • Node.js release schedule: https://github.com/nodejs/Release
    • Psalm, security analysis: https://psalm.dev/docs/security_analysis/
    • GitLab SAST: https://docs.gitlab.com/user/application_security/sast/

    Chapter 4

    Auth

    14 provisions · MUST 8 · SHOULD 1

    Decided

    Key words The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

    • One protocol-neutral library, named for what it does, not how. It returns a verified identity and leaves the session to the app (the stack's auth design).
    • The app always owns its session. Every driver ends in the app's findOrImportUser(identity), and the protocol never holds the session (the stack's auth design).
    • The gateway driver accepts only a signed assertion, never a bare header: user, attributes, issued-at, audience, an expiry, and a signature the gateway and app share (the stack's auth design). Drawbridge issues a 60 second assertion by default (assertion_ttl_seconds, 5 to 300), and SESAME refuses any assertion that lives longer than gateway.max_lifetime (300 seconds unless the app sets it).
    • Drivers: cas (the default today), gateway, oidc, oauth2, saml (opt-in), and fake for local development and tests (the stack's auth design).
    • Non-EOL PHP only, with no exceptions (the stack's auth design). PROCTOR check: php-floor.
    • The gateway's public keys reach apps as one key set file (JWKS) that holds the current key and the next one. Drawbridge writes it (keys:jwks), Playbook carries WSU's copy (public keys only), and the app points SESAME's gateway.jwks_file (SESAME_GATEWAY_JWKS_FILE) at it. An app SHOULD read that file rather than copy keys into config values, and the gateway driver never fetches keys over the network at sign-in (the stack's signing-key decision). Held by: SESAME config, which checks the file at boot: a missing file, private key material or a repeated kid stops the app.
    • The gateway's signing key MUST be rotated every 12 months, and at once when a private key could have been exposed. A retired key MUST stay in the key set for at least 5 minutes after the switch, so assertions signed just before it still verify (the stack's signing-key decision). No check exists yet. Still open: where the private keys live on Citadel and who runs the yearly rotation.
    • The saml driver is built on onelogin/php-saml, is opt-in, sets no default WSU identity provider, and requires the provider to sign its assertions (the stack's SAML decision). SESAME config: the saml block.
    • API and other stateless requests MUST be authenticated with signed, short-lived bearer tokens in an Authorization header, verified on every request. A token is signed, not merely encrypted; JSON Web Tokens are a good fit (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • Authentication MUST be checked before any content is shown or any script function runs, on every request. Deny by default: routes are protected unless listed as public, and an unauthenticated person is sent to sign in (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • When authentication or an authorization lookup fails, the app MUST fail closed: access is withheld (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • Administrative access MUST be limited to named users or roles, and access that is due to end is revoked on a regular schedule (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • Access that is due to end when a person's status changes (for example an ended employment) MUST be removed by an automated process, not by memory (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • Idle sessions MUST time out after a configurable period of inactivity (WSU developer standards, 2024). The stack's numbers are in policy/policy.json, under sessions, which is the source for them: SESAME signs a user out after 120 minutes idle and 720 minutes in all (sessions.sesame), and Drawbridge after 3600 seconds idle and 28800 seconds in all (sessions.gateway). Held by: SESAME config, session.idle_minutes (SESAME_SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES) and session.absolute_minutes (SESAME_SESSION_ABSOLUTE_MINUTES), with those defaults. An app that does not use SESAME sets its own idle limit; that is documented only.

    5

    Chapter 5

    Databases

    9 sections · 27 provisions · MUST NOT 1 · MUST 5 · SHOULD 2 · MAY 1

    Decided

    Key words The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

    §5.1 What the stack supports

    The policy lists the MySQL versions in policy/policy.json, under mysql: 5.6, 5.7, 8.0, 8.4 and 9.7, each with its active_until and security_until dates. The shared server runs 5.6, which is past security support; its security_until is 2021-02-28. Laravel 13 documents MySQL 5.7 or later, and each Laravel line in the policy records the oldest MySQL and MariaDB it needs (requires.mysql and requires.mariadb); PROCTOR 0.10.0's mysql-minimum warns when an app's declared database image is below that minimum. The conventions below keep an app working on the shared server until it is upgraded. They are a bridge, not the fix: the fix is the upgrade. Code that follows them runs unchanged on 8.4, so the move can be made With Arms Wide Open.

    §5.2 Which MySQL lines the policy lists

    The policy lists the LTS lines, 8.4 and 9.7, for current use. It keeps the older lines, 5.6, 5.7 and 8.0, only to say that they are end of life. In MySQL 8.4 and later the default authentication plugin is caching_sha2_password: mysql_native_password is disabled by default in 8.4 and removed in 9.0. An app that MUST reach a server on the older plugin MUST set the server's plugin explicitly in its database config. No check exists yet.

    §5.3 Grace period

    An app MAY stay on a database version for 90 days after it leaves support, the policy's eol_grace_days; the version is Eol through that window and EolGraceExpired the day after. The window is a bridge for the upgrade, not a second support window: the fix is still the upgrade. PROCTOR check: mysql-eol.

    • For MySQL and MariaDB the check warns and does not fail yet. While Citadel's shared server runs 5.6, an app has no supported MySQL to move to there, so a security-only, Eol or EolGraceExpired version warns, and still says to move to 8.4 or later. It starts failing past the window when Citadel offers a supported MySQL (the stack's MySQL gate decision). PROCTOR check: mysql-eol (since PROCTOR 0.8.0).

    §5.4 Names, comments and connections

    • Table and column names are descriptive. Add table and column comments (Laravel's ->comment()) where the database supports them, to say what an element is for (SHOULD) (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • The connection between the app and the database MUST be encrypted. The database account MUST have only the privileges the app needs, never an administrator account (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

    §5.5 Conventions that keep 5.6 working

    • Set Schema::defaultStringLength(191) in AppServiceProvider::boot(), before any migration runs. 5.6 caps an indexed utf8mb4 column at 767 bytes, which is 191 characters. PROCTOR check: mysql56.
    • An app MUST keep utf8mb4 and utf8mb4_unicode_ci, the defaults, and MUST NOT use an 8.0-only collation such as utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci (not yet confirmed on a 5.6 server). No check exists yet.
    • Store JSON as text or longText, with Eloquent array or json casts, and filter in PHP. 5.6 has no JSON column type. PROCTOR check: mysql56.
    • Leave use_upsert_alias unset, so upsert() uses VALUES(). The row alias that setting switches to needs MySQL 8.0.19.
    • Rename a column with raw DB::statement('ALTER TABLE ... CHANGE ...'). Avoid renameColumn and renameIndex, which emit 5.7 syntax. PROCTOR check: mysql56.
    • Use Schema::hasTable only. Column introspection is not reliable on 5.6 (not yet confirmed on a 5.6 server).
    • Skip db:show and db:monitor. PROCTOR check: mysql56.
    • An app SHOULD run one database-queue worker (or another driver if the platform offers one). 5.6 has no SKIP LOCKED, so a single worker avoids double-processing. No check exists yet.
    • Use timestamp, not date, for useCurrent(). A date column cannot take a current-timestamp default on 5.6.
    • Run migrations in CI against a real 5.6 container. SQLite-only tests pass code that 5.6 rejects.

    §5.6 Avoid until the server is upgraded

    §5.6.1 Schema

    • JSON and jsonb columns
    • Generated columns
    • renameIndex and renameColumn
    • Column introspection
    • invisible, instant and vector columns
    • InnoDB spatialIndex (needs 5.7.5, not yet confirmed on a 5.6 server)
    • DESC indexes and CHECK constraints

    §5.6.2 Queries

    • whereJson* and JSON-path updates
    • Window functions and CTEs
    • SKIP LOCKED and NOWAIT in raw SQL
    • joinLateral
    • Joined deletes with an order or a limit

    §5.6.3 Commands

    • db:show
    • db:monitor

    §5.7 Moving to 8.4

    Code that follows the conventions and avoids the patterns above runs unchanged on 8.4. The server-side large-prefix settings (innodb_large_prefix=ON, innodb_file_format=Barracuda, DYNAMIC rows) are a question for the database owners, not something an app sets (not yet confirmed on a 5.6 server). Passing ROW_FORMAT=DYNAMIC through the engine config is likewise not yet confirmed on a 5.6 server.

    Oracle moved 5.6 to Sustaining Support on 2021-02-01, so it gets no new fixes. Builds older than 5.6.46 also speak only TLS 1.0, which current hosts may refuse (not yet confirmed on a 5.6 server). Both are reasons to plan the move rather than wait for it.

    §5.8 How the stack checks it

    PROCTOR's mysql56 check flags the patterns in the avoid list above that fail on 5.6: JSON columns, generated columns, renameColumn, long indexed strings and a missing Schema::defaultStringLength(191). The rest of the list is not checked yet.

    §5.9 Sources

    • Laravel 13 database docs: https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/database
    • Laravel docs, migrations.md (index-length section): https://github.com/laravel/docs/blob/10.x/migrations.md
    • Laravel 13 migrations docs: https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/migrations
    • Laravel 13 query builder docs: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/laravel/docs/13.x/queries.md
    • Laravel database queue: https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/13.x/src/Illuminate/Queue/DatabaseQueue.php
    • Laravel schema builder: https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/13.x/src/Illuminate/Database/Schema/Builder.php
    • MySQL 5.7.7 release notes: https://dev.mysql.com/doc/relnotes/mysql/5.7/en/news-5-7-7.html
    • MySQL 5.7.8 release notes (JSON): https://dev.mysql.com/doc/relnotes/mysql/5.7/en/news-5-7-8.html
    • MySQL 5.7.6 release notes (generated columns): https://dev.mysql.com/doc/relnotes/mysql/5.7/en/news-5-7-6.html
    • MySQL 5.6 CREATE INDEX (767 and 3072 byte limits): https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.6/en/create-index.html
    • MySQL 8.0, what is new: https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/mysql-nutshell.html
    • MySQL CHECK constraints: https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/create-table-check-constraints.html
    • MySQL 5.7 INFORMATION_SCHEMA COLUMNS: https://dev.mysql.com/doc/mysql-infoschema-excerpt/5.7/en/information-schema-columns-table.html
    • MySQL RENAME INDEX worklog: https://dev.mysql.com/worklog/task/?id=6555
    • MySQL INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE (row alias from 8.0.19): https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/insert-on-duplicate.html
    • Oracle MySQL end-of-life notices: https://www.mysql.com/support/eol-notice.html
    • MySQL 5.6 TLS protocols: https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E17952_01/mysql-5.6-en/encrypted-connection-protocols-ciphers.html
    • MySQL 9.7, native pluggable authentication: https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/9.7/en/native-pluggable-authentication.html

    components.*.versions.*.active_until
    set per version
    rules.eol_grace_days
    90
    components.*.versions.*.security_until
    set per version

    6

    Chapter 6

    Runtime and headers

    8 sections · 16 provisions · MUST NOT 1 · MUST 2 · SHOULD NOT 1

    Decided

    Key words The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

    §6.1 Enforcement

    • The runtime (Baseline) is enforcement point (a): it warns, and refuses only for unsafe config (the stack's enforcement design).

    §6.2 Headers

    • Every response carries the same headers from HELMET (the stack's runtime and headers design):
      • Content-Security-Policy: the WayneUI default policy plus a per-request nonce and strict-dynamic, with frame-ancestors 'self', base-uri 'self', object-src 'none' and form-action 'self' added.
      • X-Content-Type-Options nosniff.
      • X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN.
      • Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin.
      • Permissions-Policy, with camera, geolocation, microphone, payment and usb denied by default.
      • Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy same-origin.
      • Strict-Transport-Security max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains, on HTTPS responses only.
    • Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy is off by default and opt-in, because a blanket same-site can break an app whose assets are read cross-origin (the stack's runtime and headers design). HELMET 1.0 ships that default: corp (raw PHP) or HELMET_CORP (Laravel) set to same-site, same-origin or cross-origin sends it.
    • An app SHOULD NOT weaken the default Content-Security-Policy with 'unsafe-inline' for scripts; it uses the nonce instead (the stack's runtime and headers design). PROCTOR check: csp-unsafe-inline warns on committed app config, server config or an example env file that does (PROCTOR 0.10.0).

    The headers are the setlist: the same one on every response. The HSTS encore plays only when the show is really on HTTPS.

    §6.3 Proxy trust

    • Behind a proxy the app sees the proxy's address, so X-Forwarded-Proto is honored only from a trusted proxy (the stack's runtime and headers design).
    • A platform preset (citadel or docker) names the trusted proxies; off the platform the app passes its own list. An unknown preset throws at boot (the stack's runtime and headers design).
    • No Strict-Transport-Security is sent for a request that was not really secure (the stack's runtime and headers design).

    §6.4 Sessions

    • HELMET hardens the PHP session settings before the session starts (the stack's runtime and headers design).
    • The request-forgery guard (Sec-Fetch-Site, then Origin) is optional and off by default; a rejected request gets 403 Forbidden (the stack's runtime and headers design).

    §6.5 Health

    • /up is the health endpoint HELMET answers for raw PHP apps (the stack's runtime and headers design).

    §6.6 Metrics

    • HELMET's metrics endpoint speaks the Prometheus text format and is off by default. It stays off until a Prometheus server scrapes the app; then the app turns it on with HELMET_METRICS_ENABLED=true (the stack's metrics decision). HELMET: with neither HELMET_METRICS_TOKEN nor HELMET_METRICS_ALLOW set, the endpoint answers 404 and logs a warning.
    • The scrape token MUST NOT be committed. On Citadel it goes in the app's .env through Citadel's configuration files step, which writes the file at deploy time (the stack's metrics decision). PROCTOR check: app-key (proctor/app-key/committed-env flags a committed .env).
    • On Citadel, request counts use the sqlite store for now (HELMET_METRICS_STORAGE=sqlite, with HELMET_METRICS_SQLITE_PATH on a file in the app's writable storage); the final store is picked when the stack's Prometheus server exists (the stack's metrics decision). Documented only.

    §6.7 Errors in production

    • PHP display_errors MUST be Off and log_errors On in production (Squire's deploy kit ships that php.ini; HELMET neither sets nor checks it). PROCTOR check: display-errors warns on a committed php.ini, .user.ini or .htaccess that turns display_errors on or log_errors off (PROCTOR 0.10.0).
    • Laravel APP_DEBUG MUST be false in production (WSU developer standards, 2024). The Laravel adapter writes one warning helmet.debug_enabled_in_production when it is true in the production environment. PROCTOR check: app-debug (since PROCTOR 0.10.0): it warns when a committed production env template, deploy file or CI pipeline sets APP_DEBUG to true (.env.example is the local template and is skipped).

    §6.8 Not decided here

    • The Content-Security-Policy report endpoints.

    7

    Chapter 7

    Deploy gate

    2 sections · 8 provisions

    Decided

    Key words The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

    The deploy gate runs PROCTOR against the commit being released, before it is released, and refuses EOL PHP (the stack's deploy-gate decision).

    • The deploy-time rule set is small, offline and fast: the target image's status and its PHP version against policy.json, the framework and stack package versions in composer.lock, and known advisories from a cached database (the stack's deploy-gate decision).
    • EOL fails: a deploy that regresses a rule, a new app that fails any rule, or an expired override is blocked (the stack's deploy-gate decision).
    • It ratchets: a deploy that doesn't make things worse always passes (the stack's deploy-gate decision).
    • Each rule moves through stages, report, warn, block, with dates in policy.json (the stack's deploy-gate decision).
      • The gate block holds them: default_stage (block) and stages, a list of {stage, from} entries per PROCTOR check; the latest from on or before the run date wins. It ships empty, so every check blocks until a date is agreed with the Citadel team.

    §7.1 On Citadel

    • When the Citadel team adopts it, the gate runs in the release hook: proctor gate in runGitPull(), against the fetched commit, before it is checked out (the stack's deploy-gate decision).
    • The gate is pending the Citadel team, which is still an open question. Until it is adopted, enforcement is CI on the test GitLab instance (the stack's deploy-gate decision).

    §7.2 Elsewhere

    • The same gate runs as a CI job through Preflight's proctor component, wherever the pipeline runs (first-repos).
    • Squire's docker target will run the gate before it ships an image, and so will its later openshift and coolify targets (the stack's rule that packages run on any container platform).

    In policy.json

    gate.default_stage
    "block"

    8

    Chapter 8

    CI

    8 provisions · MUST NOT 1 · MUST 2 · SHOULD 1

    Decided

    Key words The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

    • CI is enforcement point (c): a red pipeline before merge (the stack's enforcement design). PROCTOR check: ci-pipelines.
    • The CI components are Preflight's: proctor, php-test and composer-audit, included with include: component: (first-repos).
    • CI judges with deterministic commands, never with a model. A gate MUST NOT depend on a model's opinion (the stack's rule on language models). No check exists yet.
    • Components are pinned at a tag or SHA, never ~latest (first-repos). PROCTOR check: preflight-pinned.
    • The components run on the git.wayne.edu instance runner (first-repos), and every product strongly recommends the instance runner.
    • Every change lands through a merge request that another person reviews, and critical findings are addressed before merge (SHOULD for a one-person project: record the self-review in the merge request) (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • Every project MUST have a defined, well-understood change-control process with change requests; review and approval of merge requests is change control only for simple projects, and the process MUST be followed strictly (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • Known problem: the change-request procedure on Citadel is currently broken and needs fixing there; until it is fixed, record changes through reviewed merge requests and tell the Citadel team.

    9

    Chapter 9

    Accessibility

    4 sections · 9 provisions · MUST NOT 1 · MUST 1 · SHOULD 2

    Decided

    Key words The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

    §9.1 Target

    • Every public page of a stack app targets WCAG 2.2 Level AA (the stack's accessibility design).
    • W3C says content conforming to 2.2 also conforms to 2.1 and 2.0, so the target meets the WCAG 2.1 AA floor named in the ADA Title II web rule (the stack's accessibility design).

    §9.2 Components

    • WayneUI is the stack's component library; pages built from its components start from markup and tokens already checked by WayneUI's own runnable accessibility gate (the stack's accessibility design).
    • An app MUST NOT fork or restyle a WayneUI component in a way that removes focus indicators, labels or contrast (the stack's accessibility design). PROCTOR check: wayneui-forked-views catches forked views.

    §9.3 Checks

    • An automated accessibility check SHOULD run in CI on the app's key pages (the stack's accessibility design). Held by: Preflight's a11y component, below.
    • A manual keyboard and screen reader pass MUST happen before launch. An automated tool catches regressions; it is not proof of conformance, and it never replaces the pass (the stack's accessibility design). No check exists yet.
    • Preflight's a11y component (0.5.0) is the stack's CI check: it opens the app's pages in Chromium, runs axe-core in light and dark at 320 and 1280 px, and fails the pipeline on any violation. An app SHOULD add wcag22aa to its tags for the WCAG 2.2 AA target above. Held by: Preflight's a11y component (templates/a11y/template.yml).

    §9.4 Not decided here

    • Whether and when the ADA Title II web rule applies to a given WSU unit. The rule applies WCAG 2.1 AA to public entities on dates that depend on the entity's size; the answer is for WSU's counsel and accessibility office, and this chapter does not decide it.
    • Which pages need a manual audit.

    10

    Chapter 10

    Every OS

    6 provisions · MUST NOT 1 · MUST 5

    Decided

    Key words The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

    • Every developer tool MUST work on Windows, macOS and Linux (the stack's every-OS design). No check exists yet.
    • A developer script MUST ship as a .ps1 and .sh pair that do the same thing, or as one PHP command, which works the same everywhere (the stack's every-OS design). PROCTOR check: script-pair.
    • A script for Windows MUST be native PowerShell (.ps1), which never needs bash or WSL, and a script for Linux or macOS MUST be bash (.sh), written for macOS's stock bash 3.2 and its BSD tools (the stack's every-OS design). No check exists yet.
    • Every repo carries a .gitattributes with * text=auto eol=lf, and .ps1, .bat and .cmd set to CRLF. Anything that runs on a Linux host MUST be LF: on Citadel, and on OpenShift, Coolify or raw Docker elsewhere (the stack's every-OS design). PROCTOR checks: crlf-deploy-script, for deploy scripts only: it fails on a CRLF deploy script and warns when .gitattributes does not pin *.sh to LF; and gitattributes-eol (since PROCTOR 0.11.0), which warns when .gitattributes does not pin the repo's *.sh, *.conf, Dockerfile and *.Dockerfile files to eol=lf, and on a CRLF Dockerfile or .conf under deploy/ or .squire/.
    • Two paths in a repo MUST NOT differ only by letter case (Docs/Guide.md and docs/guide.md): Windows and macOS ignore case, so one checkout silently overwrites the other, and a Linux host then loads a file nobody edited (BEST_PRACTICES practice 34). PROCTOR check: case-clash, since PROCTOR 0.9.0.
    • Paths are built with the language's path functions, and subprocesses start with argument arrays, never shell strings (the stack's every-OS design). PROCTOR check: portability.

    11

    Chapter 11

    Secrets and debugging

    3 sections · 9 provisions · MUST NOT 4 · MUST 5 · SHOULD NOT 1

    Decided

    Key words The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

    §11.1 Credentials

    • Credentials (database and service passwords, API keys, tokens) MUST NOT be committed to version control, because history keeps them forever. Commit .env.example with placeholders instead. A credential that was ever committed is treated as exposed and rotated (WSU developer standards, 2024). PROCTOR checks: app-key (a committed .env or APP_KEY) and repo-url-credentials (a token in a package source URL). The general secret scan is Preflight's secret-detection component (Preflight 0.5.0), which runs Gitleaks over the tree and fails the pipeline on a match.
    • Credentials and sensitive data MUST live outside any folder the web server serves. Laravel's public/ is the only served folder; raw PHP apps serve one public/ folder the same way (WSU developer standards, 2024). PROCTOR check: served-folder (dumps, backups, logs and env files in public/).
    • The Laravel APP_KEY is a credential: whoever holds it can forge encrypted payloads, which can mean code execution. It MUST NOT be committed, a key that leaked MUST be rotated with php artisan key:generate on every environment that used it, and the session driver SHOULD NOT be cookie, which seals every session with the key (GitGuardian, exploiting public APP_KEY leaks). PROCTOR check: app-key.
    • An app MUST use its own dedicated application ID, never a person's employee or student AccessID, to reach another server or service, with the fewest permissions the task needs (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • Real values MUST come from the environment at deploy time (the Citadel dashboard or CI variables), never from a file in the repo (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

    §11.2 Errors and debug output

    • APP_DEBUG MUST be false in production (WSU developer standards, 2024). The Laravel adapter writes one warning helmet.debug_enabled_in_production when it is true in the production environment. PROCTOR check: app-debug (since PROCTOR 0.10.0), which warns when a committed production env template, deploy file or CI pipeline sets it to true.
    • Public-facing code MUST NOT display default interpreter or framework error pages to the user; show a controlled message and log the detail (WSU developer standards, 2024). Held by: HELMET, when the app turns it on. Raw PHP apps get a fixed 500 page with no exception text from the opt-in error handler (helmet_boot() with error_handler enabled) and a fixed 4xx page from helmet_client_error(); Laravel apps set HELMET_ERROR_PAGES=true for the same 4xx pages and leave 5xx to Laravel's handler, which shows no detail with APP_DEBUG false; JSON clients keep Laravel's JSON answer. The 4xx pages are on HELMET main and ship in its next release. Nothing checks that an app turned them on.
    • Logs and diagnostic output MUST NOT contain credentials or personally identifiable information such as Social Security numbers. That includes logged exceptions (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

    A leaked password is a bad encore: everyone remembers it, and nobody asked for a second showing.

    §11.3 Not decided here

    • The HELMET header rules and runtime refusals are written in runtime-and-headers.md.

    12

    Chapter 12

    Production

    3 sections · 17 provisions · MUST NOT 3 · MUST 8 · SHOULD 4

    Decided

    Key words The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

    §12.1 Environments

    • Every environment more than one person can reach follows the whole handbook; only a developer's own machine is exempt (WSU developer standards, 2024).
    • Keep at least a pre-production and a production environment, each with its own working copy of every piece, database and supporting services included (WSU developer standards, 2024).
    • Each deployment SHOULD be isolated from the others (one container per app), so one compromise does not become many. This holds on Citadel, OpenShift, Coolify and plain Docker (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • Whether a deployment is in disaster-recovery scope SHOULD be decided early, and the decision written in the README (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • Anything kept outside source control, databases included, MUST be backed up. The README MUST say how to restore one app (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • An app SHOULD be load tested in each environment where heavy use is expected (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

    §12.2 Running safely

    • The app and its scripts MUST run as a non-root, non-administrator user with the least access they need (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • The web server MUST NOT list directory contents (WSU developer standards, 2024). PROCTOR check: directory-listing warns on committed server config that turns listing on (PROCTOR 0.10.0).
    • File permissions MUST be set per path; write access for the web server is granted only to specific files or folders, and mode 777 MUST NOT be used (WSU developer standards, 2024). PROCTOR check: world-writable (chmod 777 in scripts, Dockerfiles, CI and PHP).
    • Debugging and diagnostic files, scripts, dumps and backups MUST NOT sit in the served folder (WSU developer standards, 2024). PROCTOR check: served-folder (phpinfo(), dumps, backups, logs, env files and adminer*.php under public/).
    • On failure the app MUST degrade predictably and fail closed: an authentication error withholds access (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • A person is told when something fails: a monitor calls /up on a schedule and alerts someone (WSU developer standards, 2024).
    • Logs are rotated or removed at a set interval; temporary files are cleaned up; uploaded files have a retention rule. Citadel rotates container logs; elsewhere the platform or the app MUST (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • Where it is practical, an app SHOULD record an audit trail of changes to data and of successful and failed access to sensitive data (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

    Production is the encore. Keep the lights on and the doors locked, and the band plays on.

    §12.3 Who can reach it

    • Every app MUST set robots.txt to keep spiders out unless crawling is wanted (WSU developer standards, 2024). An app that wants crawling says so in the file with Allow: / for User-agent: *; keeping spiders out is Disallow: /. PROCTOR check: robots-txt warns when a served app commits no public/robots.txt, or one that decides neither (PROCTOR 0.10.0).
    • Every app MUST limit access by network address to the audience it serves, as a second lock beside sign-in and never instead of it (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • The one named exception: the stack's own public front pages are crawlable by design (the stack's agent-ready sites decision). It is a special case for those pages, not a general exemption for public pages.

    13

    Chapter 13

    Overrides

    7 provisions · MUST NOT 1 · MUST 2

    Decided

    Key words The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

    • Overrides are named, dated and visible (the stack's version policy).
    • An app keeps a policy-overrides.json with an expiry date and a reason (the stack's version policy). PROCTOR check: overrides.
    • Check prints every override on every run, and Fleet lists them (the stack's version policy).
    • An expired override is a failure (first-repos). PROCTOR check: overrides.
    • An override runs at most rules.override_max_days days past today (90 in the policy). A longer one is a failure and does not apply. PROCTOR check: overrides.
    • An override MUST be approved by someone who did not write it. The merge request that adds or changes policy-overrides.json is the human control: the person named in approved_by approves it. In CI, PROCTOR compares approved_by with who git says wrote the entry and warns (or fails, per rules.override_self_approval, warn in the policy) on a match, or when it cannot read who did. PROCTOR check: override-approver.
    • On the Citadel side, overrides are held by Citadel admins, per app and per rule, and MUST carry an expiry, a reason and an approver. There MUST NOT be a permanent override (the stack's deploy-gate decision). No check exists yet.
